_comment: P4-17. The T1-T10 matrix: for each §3.0 threat, the control and the tests that are its evidence. One source for the named spec files beside this, for `pnpm test:security`, and for docs/security/threat-coverage.md. `runner` is how a file is run: `unit` (vitest.config.ts), `integration` (vitest.integration.config.ts, Docker) or `e2e` (Playwright, its own CI job). `gaps` are named, never hidden: each is work a later row owns.

threats.goal: Embed a stolen `pk_` on their own site
threats.control: Global-unique verified origin + server-side `Origin` check + origin-bound token

evidence.covers: Origin checked server-side, exact echo, one refusal for every wrong pair
the same check over the real accessor and policies, incl. every P2-06 bypass string
a key resolves only with its own tenant's verified origin
one origin, one tenant: the global unique index
a token presented from another origin, or with none, is refused
a real browser on an unverified origin is refused

threats.goal: Read another tenant's catalog via the API

evidence.covers: every tenant table hides, and refuses writes to, another tenant's rows
every table with a tenant_id carries a forced policy, found by reflection
every id route answers another winery's id with a plain 404
no handler reads a tenant id from the request
a tenant id in the request changes nothing, against real memberships

threats.goal: Poison the CORS allowlist with a lookalike domain
threats.control: Exact-set origin match, PSL validation, DNS/well-known verification

evidence.covers: one canonical origin per input; lookalikes, IP literals and public suffixes refused
the TXT proof, from a pinned public resolver, compared in constant time
the file proof, through guardedFetch
no verification fetch reaches our own network, rebinding included
an origin held elsewhere is refused without saying by whom

threats.control: Multi-dimension rate limits (session, IP, tenant), quota gate before model call

evidence.covers: which dimensions each endpoint draws, the month as a calendar window
each dimension trips on its own, through the real middleware
the conformance suite against the Postgres limiter, windows computed in SQL
the monthly cap is read from billed usage
a spent month is refused before the provider is built or called

gaps.what: The k6 abuse scenario that validates T4 under real concurrency

threats.goal: Steer the model via product descriptions
threats.control: Retrieved content treated as data; output allowlisted against candidate set

evidence.covers: catalogue text cannot carry a live delimiter, a comment or a fence into the prompt
the system prompt is byte-identical whatever the catalogue says
a steered answer naming products outside the candidates is cut

threats.control: Stripe webhook signature + idempotency; status never client-supplied

evidence.covers: no code outside the named writers sets a tenant's status or plan
nothing tenant-shaped is read from a request

gaps.what: Webhook idempotency: a replayed event is a no-op
Every status transition driven only by a verified event

threats.goal: XSS the seller's storefront through the widget
threats.control: Shadow DOM, text nodes only, no `innerHTML`, output sanitization

evidence.covers: hostile text renders as text, with no inline handler, and data: or vbscript: URLs are dropped
a card is filled from the catalogue, never from what the model said
the lint rule banning innerHTML in the widget is in force

threats.goal: Escalate `EDITOR` → `OWNER`, or act with no membership at all
threats.control: Declarative capability table; membership + role checked on every endpoint

evidence.covers: every (role × endpoint) pair, generated from the route table
a capability guard allows, refuses with 403, and names nothing it withholds
the capability table itself
the routes that change who can act need a fresh second factor
the last owner can be neither removed nor demoted, under concurrency

threats.control: Short TTL + `jti` + origin binding + revocation list

evidence.covers: signature, algorithm allowlist, expiry and skew
origin binding, jti revocation and the P4-06 cutoff on every call
a continuation cannot outlive its revocation
revocations are read under the tenant's policy

threats.goal: Exfiltrate a tenant's data via a hallucinated SKU
threats.control: Every returned `productId` re-validated against tenant + candidate set

evidence.covers: every returned productId is checked against this turn's candidates
another tenant's, an invented and a stale id are all dropped
retrieval returns none of another winery's wines
every card field comes from this tenant's catalogue
